extracted.intended_audience: Thomson Reuters employees, corporate directors, stakeholders, and general readers interested in news organization ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Corporate trust and editorial-independence principles that define obligations for Thomson Reuters, its employees, trustees and directors to preserve integrity, independence and freedom from bias in news and information services.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single-interest ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall at no time pass into the hands of any one interest, group or faction;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the principle of ownership independence as a safeguard for editorial independence. The page describes the creation of special ownership structures (e.g., the Reuters Founders Share Company and a single golden share) to prevent control by a single interest and to protect the Trust Principles during corporate changes (such as the 1984 public listing and later mergers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve integrity, independence and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: That the integrity, independence and freedom from bias of Thomson Reuters shall at all times be fully preserved;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as a continuous obligation on the company and its employees to act at all times with integrity, independence and freedom from bias. The Trust Principles were created to ensure these qualities remain central despite corporate changes; directors are required by charter to have due regard to these principles when performing their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply unbiased and reliable news services
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall supply unbiased and reliable news services to newspapers, news agencies, broadcasters and other media subscribers and to businesses, governments, institutions, individuals and others with whom Thomson Reuters has or may have contracts;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the expected product quality and audience scope: news and information must be both unbiased and reliable and provided to a wide set of clients (media organizations, businesses, governments, institutions, individuals). This functions as an editorial and service-quality standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider multiple interests beyond the media
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall pay due regard to the many interests which it serves in addition to those of the media;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs the organization to weigh the diverse interests of its broad set of users and stakeholders (not solely media customers) when carrying out its services—an explicit stakeholder-consideration standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous development to maintain leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: That no effort shall be spared to expand, develop and adapt the news and other services and products of Thomson Reuters so as to maintain its leading position in the international news and information business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates proactive improvement and adaptation of services and products to retain competitive and editorial leadership; functions as a strategic quality and innovation expectation for the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance safeguard via Founders Share Company and Trustees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reuters Founders Share Company (directors known as Trustees) holds a single Founder Share and was created to safeguard the Trust Principles; it supported corporate actions conditional on protecting those principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the institutional mechanism (founders share and Trustees) established in 1984 and maintained after subsequent mergers (including 2008 adoption by the combined company) to ensure the Trust Principles are upheld. Includes historical context: the Founders Share Company agreed to support acquisitions only where Trust Principles would be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directors' duty to regard the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter documents require Thomson Reuters directors, in the performance of their duties, to have due regard to the Reuters Trust Principles, by the proper exercise of their powers and in accordance with their other duties as directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a legal/corporate-duty requirement: directors must consider and give weight to the Trust Principles when exercising their powers and fulfilling director responsibilities, embedding the principles into corporate governance and decision-making.
